newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to renew oil import deal with Iran.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to renew oil import deal with Iran.

text.p: Turkey will renew from April its oil import agreement with Iran for at least 4.5 million tonnes annually -- the amount which it currently imports from its neighbour, a senior Turkish energy official said on Friday.
"In our talks with the Iranian delegation, we will conclude the renewal of the oil import deal, with effect from April," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
"The new agreement will be for 4.5 million tonnes, like the current agreement which ends in April, or a little bit more than that," he said.

Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, accompanied by Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and several other senior officials, have been in Turkey since Thursday for trade and political talks.
Their visit was preceded by joint economic commission meetings between officials from both countries in Ankara.
Officials said a series of agreements would be signed in Ankara on Saturday that include meaures to boost trade and political ties between the two neighbours.

Asked about a plan to launch a preliminary study for a pipeline to carry Iranian oil through Turkey, the official said: "The two sides only mentioned an intention. There is nothing tangible at this stage."
Iran and Turkey will build a pipeline to carry Iranian gas to Turkey from 1998 under a 23-year, $23-billion deal.
Turkey imports about 27 million tonnes of crude oil annually, most of which comes from Saudi Arabia.
